$why: A change to shared logic, data, permissions or a kernel rule breaks what other work stands on, and a red there found only at the batch's merge check is found after other builders stacked work on it (ISS-1061; owner, 2026-11-07: check wide early on shared logic, billing, permissions or data). `pnpm test:changed` runs the direct core integration tests of a change touching any path below with no --integration, and prints the path and its reason. Patterns are repo-relative, `*` within a segment and `**` across; an entry matching no tracked file is refused by name.

paths.reason: a migration changes the schema every query runs on, and only an integration test runs it over a real Postgres
the Drizzle schema every query is typed against must match what the migrations build
the kernel's transaction flag is what the status triggers let through; a wrong one blocks or opens every status write
the one permission vocabulary every can() check in core asks
who may act: roles, grants, memberships and the agent fence
kernel rule pat_fence: an account route a fenced token may not reach (PAT_ACCOUNT_ROUTE)
token verification, scope and grant narrowing: what a personal access token reaches
kernel rule pat_fence: a fenced token reaches only its own project (PAT_PROJECT_OUTSIDE_FENCE, PAT_ACCOUNT_ROUTE)
the door every token-authenticated request passes
what each route and tool declares it needs, which the permission check enforces
kernel rule pat_fence: an issue's requirement read across a token's fence
kernel rule pat_fence: an issue's design read across a token's fence
every status machine as data: the edges the one kernel transition writes along
the issue machine: its statuses, edges and the guards each edge names
the one kernel transition every status write goes through, and its gated-move record
KERNEL_RULES and the gate profiles: what no project setting can turn off
kernel rule transition_evidence and run_holder: the issue transition guards and their refusals (ILLEGAL_TRANSITION, NOT_THE_HOLDER, NO_HOLDER)
kernel rule transition_evidence: where an issue move is applied through the machine
kernel rule transition_evidence: a recovery move held to the machine's legal edges
kernel rule transition_evidence: a failed criterion's return move held to the machine's legal edges
kernel rule transition_evidence: a parked issue's move needs its reason (TRANSITION_REASON_REQUIRED)
kernel rule merged: no awaiting_release without a recorded merge (MERGE_NOT_RECORDED, MERGE_DESIGN_ONLY)
kernel rule close_in_scope: whether a closed issue's work is live is read from the release record here (holdingReleaseRunsSql), never from closed
kernel rule close_in_scope: only the holder or a claiming release closes, and an unmet criterion with nowhere to go is refused (NOT_THE_HOLDER, CLOSE_CRITERION_UNPLACED)
kernel rule close_in_scope: a filing cannot close an issue that has not shipped (CLOSE_ONLY_BY_RELEASE)
kernel rule close_in_scope: a design-only issue closes only once its design is approved (DESIGN_NOT_DELIVERED)
kernel rule close_in_scope: the recorded landing a release claims before it closes an issue
kernel rule close_in_scope: a beta mirror closes only what carries its merge (CLOSE_REQUIRES_SHIPPED)
kernel rule review_by_builder: a recorded review is never the builder's own (REVIEW_BY_BUILDER)
kernel rule verdict_shape: a verdict names a known criterion and carries no secret (VERDICT_CRITERION_UNKNOWN, VERDICT_SECRET)
kernel rule verdict_shape: verdicts read off events name a known criterion (VERDICT_CRITERION_UNKNOWN)
kernel rule requirement_proven: a requirement reads delivered only where every criterion is proven (REQUIREMENT_CRITERIA_UNPROVEN, REQUIREMENT_NO_LIVE_ISSUE)
